factor_cards.verdict: KEEP — weight frozen, do not raise
factor_cards.numbers: Brier on 438 lined player stats: base 0.2812, grades off 0.2812, half 0.2816, doubled 0.2826. Off helped rush attempts (0.2453 → 0.2366, n=33) and hurt receptions (0.2687 → 0.2706, n=142). Doubling was worse in all 6 markets.
factor_cards.why: Net effect is zero within noise on one week. Doubling is clearly worse, so the trench weight stays at 15% of efficiency and is not raised. Run-game trench stays on watch: if rush attempts improve again with it off next week, it gets cut.

factor_cards.factor: Raw sim probability vs the market
factor_cards.numbers: Brier on priced board lines: sim 0.2587 vs no-vig market 0.2519. By market — receptions sim 0.2461 vs market 0.2515 (sim better); rush yds 0.29 vs 0.25; rec yds 0.2561 vs 0.25; pass yds 0.2565 vs 0.2503.
factor_cards.why: Each market now blends the sim toward the no-vig price with a learned weight (shrunk toward 50/50 so one week can't swing it): completions 0.54, pass_att 0.54, pass_td 0.59, pass_yds 0.41, rec_yds 0.33, receptions 0.72, rush_att 0.5, rush_rec_yds 0.3, rush_yds 0.3.

factor_cards.numbers: Board overs went 81-117 (40.9%, -26.87u); unders 86-73 (54.1%, 21.95u). Week 9 overs were also over-predicted (54.6% sim vs 50.0% actual, 212 bets).
factor_cards.why: Two straight weeks of overs landing under the sim. Overs now give back half the measured gap, capped at 4 points.

factor_cards.numbers: Week 10 sim backtest (13 games, 438 lined stats, 3 seeds x 4,000 draws): overall Brier base 0.2817 vs blitz-only 0.2821; QB pass yds 0.2864 → 0.2852 (MAE 83.356 → 83.117); completions 0.3085 → 0.3091; rec yds 0.2901 → 0.2911. Out-of-sample check on 175 QB games (2026 weeks 4–11, rates from earlier weeks only): the QB's blitz split made the forecast worse in every piece — comp% error +2.801%, YPA +1.157%, sack rate +5.751%. A defense's raw blitz rate does correlate with lower QB YPA vs his own baseline (r = -0.157), but the per-QB blitz splits point the wrong way too often.
factor_cards.why: Wired end to end: every defense now carries its 2026 blitz rate and every QB with 40+ dropbacks carries his vs-blitz comp/YPA/sack split, in both the Python engine and the in-app sim. The evidence says the QB blitz splits add noise, so the weight is 0 (learning.json sim_factors.weights.blitz). It's re-tested each review and turns back on if it starts beating the base.

factor_cards.factor: Defensive pressure vs QB under pressure
factor_cards.verdict: KEEP for YPA and sacks (QB split at 50%), ZERO for completions and scrambles
factor_cards.numbers: Week 10 sim backtest: overall Brier base 0.2817 vs pressure-matchup 0.2823, both 0.2826, final setting 0.2821; QB pass yds 0.2864 → 0.285 (final 0.2857, side hit 0.436 → 0.474); completions 0.3085 → 0.3092; QB rush yds 0.2714 → 0.2734. Out-of-sample on 175 QB games: YPA error -0.08% with the QB's own split and -0.193% with league-average sensitivity; sack-rate error -0.12% / -0.242%; comp% got worse (+1.079%) and scrambles got worse (+0.263%). Defense pressure rate vs QB YPA residual r = -0.12; vs sack-rate residual r = 0.072.
factor_cards.why: Each defense's 2026 pressure rate (PFR times_pressured ÷ dropbacks faced) above or below league shifts the QB's pressured share. The change is that extra share times the QB's 2025 pressured-minus-clean gap, blended 50/50 with the league gap, then capped: YPA ±0.30, sack rate ±1.2 pts. Comp% and scramble pieces are zeroed because they made forecasts worse. Effects are small — a few pass yards per QB — and inside seed noise on one sim week (±0.001 Brier), so this stays on probation.
